prompt: I've finished story S01 (bulk discount): I changed src/discount.py and added tests/test_discount.py. The story is in .harness/runs/2026-10-30-bulk-discount/stories/S01.md. Write up the claims for the story judge.

expectations.text: The claims are written to claims/S01.md in the story's run folder, and no other project file changes

judged.question: Did the run write its claims to claims/S01.md in the story's run folder, and leave every other file as it was?
judged.pass: Yes when that one file is new and nothing else in the project was edited or added.
judged.fail: No when the claims are elsewhere, missing, or any source, docs or config file changed.

pass: A new claims/S01.md next to the story, with the code and docs untouched.
fail: The claims in CLAIMS.md at the root, or an edit to the code while writing them.

expectations.text: The claims file has the six claims headings in their order

judged.question: Are the level 2 headings of the claims file exactly Request, Requirements, Standards, Out of scope, Files changed and Not verified, in that order?
judged.pass: Yes when those six headings appear once each, in that order, and no other level 2 one.
judged.fail: No when one is missing, renamed, moved or another level 2 heading is added.

pass: Six headings from Request down to Not verified, as listed.
fail: Headings Summary, Criteria and Evidence instead.

expectations.text: Every file listed under Files changed has its true line count

judged.question: Does every line under Files changed name a file with its true line count?
judged.pass: Yes when each line is a path with the number of lines the file really has.
judged.fail: No when a count is wrong, a line is not a file entry, or the section lists nothing.

pass: A list of the two changed files, each with its real count.
fail: A count that is off by a few lines, or a sentence instead of a list.

expectations.text: Every file and line the claims cite exists

judged.question: Does every path:line the claims cite name a project file, by its path from the project root, and a line it has?
judged.pass: Yes when each cited line exists in the cited file.
judged.fail: No when a cited file is missing, is named without its folder, or is shorter than the line.

pass: A cited line inside the function that does the work.
fail: A cited line past the end of the file, or a bare file name without its folder.

expectations.text: The tests are run while writing the claims

judged.question: Did the run itself run the project's tests before writing the claims?
judged.pass: Yes when the command list shows a test command run by this run.
judged.fail: No when no test command ran, so any result in the claims was not fresh.

pass: The command list holds the unittest command the project uses.
fail: The command list shows only file reads and the write of the claims.

expectations.text: AC-1, AC-2 and AC-3 are each met, with the code line and the test that prove it

contract.quote: AC-1: An order whose subtotal is 100.00 or more is discounted by 10%

judged.question: Does each of AC-1, AC-2 and AC-3 have status met, a path:line in src/discount.py and a test named by its function name?
judged.pass: Yes when all three have the status met, a cited code line and a named passing test.
judged.fail: No when one is missing, has another status, or cites no code line or no test.

pass: AC-2 is met, cites the quantity check in src/discount.py and names test_negative_quantity_is_rejected.
fail: AC-3 says only that rounding is done, with no line and no test.

expectations.text: The claims quote the result of the run of the tests: four tests, all passing

judged.question: Do the claims quote the test command's own result, showing four tests run and none failed?
judged.pass: Yes when the evidence quotes the count of four and the OK line of that run.
judged.fail: No when the claims say the tests pass without quoting a run, or quote another count.

expectations.text: Files changed lists src/discount.py and tests/test_discount.py

judged.question: Does Files changed list both src/discount.py and tests/test_discount.py, and no file the change did not touch?
judged.pass: Yes when both are listed and nothing else but the claims file itself.
judged.fail: No when either is missing or an untouched file is listed.

pass: The two files, each with its count.
